newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates fall across the board.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates fall across the board.

text.p: Mexico's Cetes rates fell across the yield curve at the primary auction on Tuesday, as better long-term inflation expectations and unchanged U.S. monetary conditions bolstered spirits, analysts said.
Demand was strong at the auction as the bellwether one-month paper fell 10 basis points to 23.28 percent.
The three-month paper was assigned 55 basis points lower at 26.75 percent, while the six-month paper was assigned 52 basis points lower at 28.16 percent.
One-year paper was assigned at 28.03 percent, compared with 29.18 percent the week before, Banco de Mexico said.
Demand was 15.48 billion pesos this week compared with 10.95 billion last week.
The auction closed a few minutes after the Federal Open Market Committee released its decision not to change U.S. interest rates, and that helped Mexican rates to decline, analysts said.
Earlier this week, some market players had expected rates to rise.
"It was what people were waiting for, but once the news of the Fed came out, everything changed," said one dealer.
Analysts said that expectations of weaker long-term inflation gave strength to the decline in longer-term rates.
"We are expecting a slight bubble for the end of the year but in general the expectations for the long term are good and this has created a better demand for paper," said another dealer.
At the start of the year the one-month Cetes paper was yielding closer to 40 percent, so the rate decline has been sharp, as inflationary pressures have eased.

Indicating greater confidence on inflation, Bear Stearns on Tuesday said it raised its estimate for 1996 Mexico Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to 4.5 percent from 3.5 percent, and reduced its consumer inflation estimate to 27 percent from 31 percent.
It also raised its Mexico GDP growth estimate for 1997 to 4.0 percent from 3.3 percent and lowered its 1997 inflation estimate to 15 percent from 18 percent.
